title: Proper source direct image identifies nearby-cycle comparison defects
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be finite-type morphisms with $h$ proper, and put $f=gh$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $\Lambda$ be finite, killed by an integer invertible on $S$, and let $L\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$. For $T\to S$ and a geometric specialization $b\to a$ in $S$ lifted to $b_T\to a_T$ in $T$, write $\Psi^f_{a,b}L=i_a^*Rj_{b,*}L$ on $X_a$, where the maps are formed after strict localization at $a$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Write $C^f_T(L)$ for the cone on $X_{a_T}$ of $\Psi^f_{a,b}L|_{X_{a_T}}\to\Psi^{f_T}_{a_T,b_T}L_T$, using the ordinary comparison [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Define $C^g_T$ similarly on $Y_{a_T}$. Proper base change identifies $L'_T=(Rh_*L)|_{Y_T}$ with $Rh_{T,*}L_T$ and gives a canonical identification
$$Rh_{a_T,*}C^f_T(L)\simeq C^g_T(Rh_*L).$$
It respects further base changes and is the comparison obtained from the ordinary counit-defined maps. For $h$ finite, exactness and the finite geometric-stalk product formula imply: $P_r(f,L)$ implies $P_r(g,Rh_*L)$ for every $r$ [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data].
